bullets: Stocks surged Wed as Democrats won Congress; VIX fell ~20% to 16.6, but Thu futures dip (Nasdaq -1%) on an Asia chip selloff (Kospi -4.6%).
Oil fell further overnight (Brent near $88-94) on hopes a weaker Trump faces pressure to end the Iran conflict, easing inflation fears.
10Y yield eased toward 4.89%; gold and bitcoin both higher, signaling risk appetite intact despite the equity-futures pullback.
Heavy data: jobless claims today 8:30am ET; NFP, unemployment rate and consumer sentiment due Fri Nov 6 - key for Fed path.

CRWD.why: Drop tracks a broad software/cybersecurity selloff (Fortinet earnings, AI-capex and valuation-compression fears across the group), not CRWD-specific news; rvol near 1x confirms no idiosyncratic volume spike.
CRWD.bull: Sector-wide selloff, not CRWD-specific; Deutsche Bank just raised PT to $300 with a fresh Buy rating.
CRWD.bear: Richly valued cybersecurity names stay vulnerable to further multiple compression if AI-capex worries persist.
CRWD.catalysts: none found in next 7 trading days; next earnings well outside window (ed=18)

HPQ.why: Bulk of the sell-off tracks a sector-wide PC-slump/memory-shortage warning (Dell -11%, HPE -7%, SMCI -7% same day), but HP also named an outsider pharma CEO (ex-GSK Walmsley), adding execution-risk uncertainty on top of the sector move.
HPQ.bull: Drop is mostly industry-wide (Intel memory-shortage/PC-slump warning hit Dell and HPE too); shares already bounced 5.7% off lows.
HPQ.bear: New outsider CEO with no PC-industry background adds leadership uncertainty just as memory costs squeeze hardware margins.
HPQ.catalysts: none in next 7 trading days; Q4 FY26 earnings Nov 24 falls outside the hold window

RRC.why: Drop tracks energy-sector/gas-price weakness, plus RRC's pending fixed-ratio stock merger with EQT ties its price to EQT (which fell on integration/low-gas-price worries). No company-specific damage found; both recent analyst moves raised price targets.

RRC.bear: As a fixed-ratio merger target, RRC's price is now tethered to EQT, so further EQT/gas-price weakness caps the bounce.
